outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Large Language Models and the Need for Quantization
outline.description: Sets the stage by reviewing the rapid growth of LLMs, their performance achievements, and the challenges posed by their computational and environmental costs. Introduces quantization as a primary strategy for addressing these issues.
subtopics: Evolution of LLMs: from early models to today’s billions‑parameter transformers
Hardware bottlenecks: memory bandwidth, compute energy, and latency
Overview of model compression techniques (pruning, distillation, quantization)
Post‑training quantization vs. training‑time quantization
Motivation for moving beyond 4‑bit and toward 1‑bit representations

outline.description: Provides the mathematical background needed to understand low‑bit quantization, including uniform vs. non‑uniform schemes, rounding strategies, and error analysis.
subtopics: Quantization theory: mapping real numbers to discrete codebooks
Uniform quantization, symmetric vs. asymmetric intervals
Rounding functions: stochastic, deterministic, and round‑clip
Statistical measures for quantization error (MSE, signal‑to‑noise ratio)
Impact of quantization on matrix multiplication

outline.chapter_title: The BitNet Architecture: From FP16 Transformers to 1‑bit Linear Layers
outline.description: Describes the original BitNet design that replaces standard linear layers with BitLinear, explaining how integer additions replace floating‑point multiplications.
subtopics: Recap of the standard Transformer block (nn.Linear, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE)
Design of BitLinear: ternary weight representation and integer arithmetic
Advantages of eliminating multiplications in matrix multiplication
Integration with existing LLM toolkits (Hugging Face, vLLM, llama.cpp)
Limitations of pure 1‑bit (binary) weight schemes

outline.chapter_title: BitNet b1.58: Architecture and Training Details
outline.description: Introduces the 1.58‑bit variant, explaining the ternary weight set {−1,0,+1}, the modified quantization function, and training hyper‑parameters.
subtopics: Why add a zero weight? Feature filtering and expressive power
AbsMean quantization function and RoundClip operator
Computation of scaling factor γ (average absolute weight)
Activation quantization: symmetric int8 range \([-Q_b,Q_b]\)
Adopted LLaMA components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings, bias removal
(Optional) Pseudocode for forward pass of a BitLinear layer

outline.description: Covers practical aspects of training from scratch with ternary weights, including optimizer choices, learning‑rate schedules, and token data pipelines.
subtopics: Optimizers compatible with extreme weight quantization (AdamW with weight decay)
Gradient handling for ternary weights (straight‑through estimator)
"Warmup" and cosine decay schedules used on RedPajama data
"Token budget" considerations: 100B vs 2T token regimes
"Mixed precision" during backpropagation (weights ternary, activations int8)
"Regularisation" techniques to prevent collapse to all zeros

outline.description: Describes the datasets, model sizes, hardware platforms, and evaluation metrics employed in the paper.
subtopics: "Training corpus": RedPajama (100B tokens) and StableLM token recipe (2T tokens)
"Model scales": 3B, 3.9B, 7B, 13B, 70B parameter families
"Baseline": FP16 LLaMA models trained under identical conditions
"Evaluation tasks": perplexity on WikiText2 & C4; zero‑shot accuracy on ARC‑E/​C, Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ etc.
"Hardware": NVIDIA A100 GPUs; FasterTransformer inference engine; Ladder 2‑bit kernels
"Metrics": latency per token, GPU memory consumption, throughput (tokens/s), estimated energy per operation

outline.chapter_title: Performance Results: Accuracy vs. Efficiency Trade‑offs
outline.description: Presents the main empirical findings—how BitNet b1.58 matches or exceeds FP16 baselines in perplexity and downstream tasks while delivering large speedups and memory reductions.
subtopics: "Perplexity comparison" across model sizes (tables & plots)
"Zero‑shot task accuracy" trends and Pareto fronts
"Latency & memory" measurements; scaling behavior up to 70B parameters
"Throughput gains" with pipeline parallelism on multi‑GPU setups
"Energy estimation" methodology (FP16 mul/add vs INT8 add) and results

outline.\tdescription: Analyzes the new scaling relationship introduced by the authors that links model size with inference cost at 1.58 bits.
\tsubtopics: "Empirical scaling curves" for latency,memory,and energy versus parameter count

outline.\tdescription: Discusses how BitNet b1.58 enables new use cases such as edge/mobile inference, long-context handling and MoE integration.
\tsubtopics: "Memory bandwidth & KV cache reduction" for longer sequences

outline.\tdescription: Explores how the computation paradigm shift motivates specialized accelerators.
\tsubtopics: "Contrast between FP16/FP32 tensor cores and integer addition units "
"Design considerations for a dedicated 1-bit/1.58-bit accelerator (sparse ternary storage, zero-skipping) "

outline.\tchapter_title: Limitations, Open Questions & Future Research Directions
outline.\tdescription: Critically examines what remains unresolved in the paper and outlines promising avenues for further study.
\tsubtopics: "Effect of zero weights on representation capacity "
"Quantisation of activations beyond int8 – toward full 1-bit pipelines "

outline.\tchapter_title: Hands‑On Tutorial: Building and Evaluating a BitNet b1.58 Model
outline.\tdescription: Step‑by‑step guide for students to reproduce a small‐scale BitNet b1.58 model using open‑source tools.
\tsubtopics: "Environment setup: PyTorch + HuggingFace Transformers + custom BitLinear module "
"Training a 300M parameter prototype on a subset of RedPajama "
"Evaluating perplexity on WikiText2 and a few zero‑shot tasks "

outline.\tdescription: Recaps the key takeaways about 1.58-bit LLMs and projects their impact on AI research and industry.
